outcome: histopathological changes in liver and kidney
morphometric analysis (body weight, crown rump length, tail length)
cohort: Pregnant female Swiss albino mice were exposed to different doses of cypermethrin and carbaryl daily for eighteen days during gestation, and their fetuses were recovered via Cesarean section.
finding: Higher dose cypermethrin (7.5 mg/g b.w.) caused significant reduction in fetal body weight (311.47 mg), crown rump length (11.23 mm), and tail length (7.25 mm) with arrested growth, as well as teratological effects and various histopathological changes in the liver and kidney of the developing fetuses.
followup_time: Observation on eighteenth day of gestation
birth_weight: 311.47 mg (fetal body weight in high dose cypermethrin group)
